title: Houthis strike Saudi oil infrastructure as Riyadh intensifies attacks on Yemen | CNN
byline: Billy Stockwell; Ibrahim Dahman; Mohammed Tawfeeq
html:
Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides.

A projectile struck an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s southwestern Jazan region on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several others, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. The strike sparked a fire and temporarily suspended some operations at the facility, the ministry said.

The attack came a day after the Houthis claimed to have struck Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery at Ras Tanura. Satellite imagery taken Wednesday showed a huge plume of black smoke rising from the coastal peninsula following the attack.

The Houthi-controlled armed forces said the attack caused a fire at Ras Tanura, part of one of the world’s largest crude oil export terminals, in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. A shipping source told CNN Thursday that oil loadings at the terminal were suspended after the attack, though it was unclear whether they have resumed.

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, with falling debris but no reported injuries.

Ras Tanura has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day and is part of a broader complex that housed Saudi Arabia’s main crude export terminal before the US-Iran war began.

Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNN.

The Houthis also claimed responsibility for a strike Wednesday on Riyadh’s King Abdullah Economic City that Saudi authorities said wounded 11 people. An eyewitness told CNN that Saudi Arabia’s trillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund, is headquartered inside the targeted skyscraper.

The Saudi-led coalition said in a later statement Wednesday that the strike was carried out by a Houthi drone and vowed a “firm response.”

Strikes intensify in Yemen

Saudi-led forces meanwhile have stepped up attacks across Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen.

On Thursday, the coalition said it carried out a “precision military operation” against Houthi capabilities, destroying 50 targets it described as legitimate military targets across Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada governorates.

A day earlier, the coalition said it attacked “operational capabilities” at the Houthi-controlled Hodeidah port and destroyed targets in Saada and Amran governorates.

The Houthi-controlled armed forces, meanwhile, said Saudi warplanes and missiles carried out 109 strikes over the previous 24 hours across Yemen including in Sanaa and Hodeidah.

The Houthi-controlled health ministry in Sanaa said Thursday that at least 19 civilians had been killed and 25 others wounded in Saudi strikes over the previous 48 hours across several parts of Yemen.

CNN has not been able to independently verify the claims about the strikes or casualties.

Crown prince’s US visit

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted infrastructure in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, including Riyadh’s financial district. Riyadh’s international airport was also hit several times last month, killing more than a dozen people.

The escalating attacks come as Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is planning his first trip to the United States since the Iran war began, where he is expected to attend next month’s G20 summit in Miami, Florida, according to a source familiar with the plans. Saudi officials have not yet publicly confirmed his attendance.

Saudi Arabia has sought US support in strengthening its defenses as it faces continued Houthi missile and drone attacks.

The planned visit would set up the first in person meeting between US President Donald Trump and Prince bin Salman since the outbreak of the war.

Fighting between the Houthi group and the Saudi-led coalition reignited in July after years of relative calm brought about by a 2022 UN-brokered ceasefire. Clashes intensified in recent months after the militant group made an advance toward the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait in September, threatening a new front in the Iran war.

CNN’s Tim Lister, Jennifer Hansler, Kathleen Magramo and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.
summary: Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis are trading increasingly intense strikes on strategic sites, including oil infrastructure and ports, marking a sharp escalation in fighting between the two sides.
